item.title: “The Tender Land” by Aaron Copland — Sun Oct 18, 3:00 PM — Musical Arts Center
item.description: The Tender Land By Aaron Copland COMING OF AGE Considered one of Copland’s finest scores and his only full-length opera, the piece was inspired by James Agee and Walker Evans’ book Let Us Now Praise Famous Men. Set in the Depression-era Midwest, it tells the story of an isolated girl who, on the eve of high-school graduation, must decide how to live her life. Commissioned by Rodgers and Hammerstein in the early ‘50s as part of a project to support American opera. Copland, celebrated for works like Appalachian Spring and Billy the Kid, was a natural fit for a story rooted in rural American life. The work premiered in 1954 at New York City Opera to lukewarm reception. Copland then substantially revised the work in 1955, tightening it from two acts into a more streamlined version. Today, The Tender Land is regarded as an important American opera, admired for its lyrical, folk-inflected score. Presented as a Concert Opera, with orchestra onstage. Artistic Staff Conductor George Manah

item.title: It Was Just An Accident | Arthouse Now — Sun Oct 18, 4:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Mechanic Vahid is jarringly reminded of his time in an Iranian prison for being branded a "dissident" when he has a chance encounter with Eghbal, a man he strongly suspects to be his sadistic jailhouse captor. Panicked, Vahid rounds up some of his fellow ex-prisoners to try and confirm Eghbal's identity and determine what to do next. Panahi creates a deeply felt moral thriller, combining high stakes tension with unexpected humor and thoughtful, yet devastating, questions regarding persecution and revenge. [103 min; thriller, drama; Persian with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar, Visit Bloomington

item.title: Dersu Uzala | Michael A. McRobbie's Choice — Sun Oct 18, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Epic in form, intimate in scope, and set in the forests of Eastern Siberia at the turn of the century, Dersu Uzala is a moving story of the friendship that grows between an aging hunter and a Russian surveyor. Based on a memoir by renowned Russian explorer Vladimir Klavdiyevich Arsenyev, Kurosawa's romantic hymn to nature and the human spirit is perhaps the most persuasive argument for the immense power of nature and the beauty found in simplicity. [142 min; adventure, drama; Russian and Mandarin with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar, Visit Bloomington

item.title: THURSDAY MUSIC NIGHT: THE HOT CLUB OF BTOWN! — Thu Oct 22, 6:00 PM — Juniper Art Gallery
item.description:
Juniper is thrilled to host an evening of fabulous Jazz Manouche with the new quartet, The Hot Club of Btown! Featured musicians are Steve Mascari, Ingrid Matthews, Alan Bent, and Craig Coley.
A brief definition of this genre of music:
Jazz manouche is a musical idiom inspired by the Romani jazz guitarist Jean "Django" Reinhardt (1910–1953), in conjunction with the French jazz violinist Stéphane Grappelli (1908–1997), as expressed by their group the Quintette du Hot Club de France. The style has its origins in France and the Manouche clan of Romanis and has remained popular amongst this clan.
This is sure to be an evening filled with truly exceptional music that will uplift all in attendance! Do not miss this performance!

item.title: Appetizers & Opportunities with CDFI Friendly — Tue Oct 27, 4:00 PM — Amplify Bloomington (Dimension Mill)
item.description:
CDFI Friendly Bloomington’s Board of Directors invites you to its annual event, bringing together residents, advocates, and regional community development partners to explore the role of Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) investment in our region. Come network, celebrate CFB’s impact, learn about its growth, and meet CDFI and community development partners.
The program begins at 4:00 pm with two panel discussions and regional community development highlights. “Small Business, Big Impact” looks under the hood of small business lending, sharing resources and best practices for entrepreneurs across the Indiana Uplands and CFB region. “Affordability in Real Time” goes beyond housing to discuss community development lending and the everyday economic challenges and opportunities our neighbors face.
A networking reception follows at 5:30 pm.
Please RSVP by October 23. Questions? Contact John Zody at john@cdfifriendlybtown.org mailto:john@cdfifriendlybtown.org .
Source: Pil
